description: The spectrum of Ad without the oscillator: it puts out one polyphonic pitch and two polyphonic amplitudes, one channel per partial, for driving your own oscillators and VCAs

params.text: Sets which octave the fundamental falls in, -5 to 2, always snapped to a whole octave
Sets the spacing of the partials in units of the fundamental: at 1 the spectrum is harmonic, below 1 it is squeezed, above 1 stretched, and at 0 every partial lands on one frequency
Sets how many partials are generated, 1 to 15
Left of centre it tilts the weight of the spectrum towards the low partials; right of centre the weights go flat and the lowest partial climbs instead
Sieves partials out: turned up from the middle it removes the proper multiples of 2, then 3, then 5, leaving the primes; turned down it removes the primes from the top, leaving the octaves
Sets how long the amplitude CV takes to travel from one partial to the next, up to 4 seconds; fully clockwise it freezes the buffer
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, on the stretch CV
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, on the number of partials CV
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, on the tilt CV
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, on the sieve CV
Restarts the spectrum and draws fresh delays for the random buffer order

inputs.text: Transposes the whole spectrum at a volt per octave, added to the octave knob; only the first channel is read
Adds to the stretch knob through its attenuverter, a volt covering a tenth of the knob's travel at full attenuation
Adds to the number of partials knob through its attenuverter, a volt covering a fifth of the knob's travel at full attenuation; pushed below zero it also flips the sign of the stretch
Adds to the tilt knob through its attenuverter, a volt covering a tenth of the knob's travel at full attenuation
Adds to the sieve knob through its attenuverter, a volt covering a tenth of the knob's travel at full attenuation
The CV recorded into the four-second buffer that sets the partial amplitudes; patching this switches the amplitude section on
Adds to the amp delay knob, a volt covering a tenth of its travel
Steps the buffer on each reading above 2.5V, which turns the amp delay knob into a clock divider rather than a time
A reading above 2.5V restarts the spectrum

outputs.text: The pitch of each partial, a volt per octave, one channel per partial
The amplitude of each partial for the left channel, one channel per partial
The amplitude of each partial for the right channel, one channel per partial

notes: this module makes no sound; patch the pitch output to an oscillator and an amplitude output to a VCA, both of them polyphonic, and the oscillator through the VCA
every input here is read on its first channel only, however many the cable carries
the module resets and stops while all three of its outputs are unpatched
Bufke is its expander and goes immediately to the right
menu: Quantize stretch: Continuous, Consonants, Harmonics — snaps the stretch after the knob and its CV are added; Consonants snaps to pure intervals, Harmonics to whole numbers
Stereo mode: Mono, Soft-panned, Hard-panned — spreads the partials across the two amplitude outputs
CV buffer order: Low→high, High→low, Random — sets the order the amplitude CV travels through the partials
Empty buffer on reset — clears the amplitude buffer on a reset instead of leaving what is already in it
Channels — sets how many polyphony channels the three outputs carry, 1 to 16
